# EvLoading

> A loading indicator communicates that content or an action is in progress, reassuring the user that the system is working and reducing perceived wait time.

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Loading**, frame `4282:80578` (Loading). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Show during async waits: spinner/pulse for short indeterminate waits, skeleton while content loads in place, progress bar for measurable tasks, logo for full-page app boot.

### When not to use

- Don't show a loader for instant actions (<300ms) — it causes flicker. Don't block the whole screen when only part of it is loading; prefer an inline skeleton.

### Do

- Match the indicator to the wait: use skeletons that mirror the final layout, and a progress bar when completion can be measured.

### Don't

- Don't mix multiple loader types in one view, and don't leave a spinner running indefinitely — show an error or timeout if the wait exceeds expectations.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvLoading`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-loading">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:loading` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
